files.description: Which files to scan for imports, whatever their language.

languages.description:
The languages to scan, each in a table of its own. A language is
enabled when its table is written, even if empty. Without a
`[languages]` table, the default languages are enabled with their
defaults; an empty one enables nothing, which is an error.

analysis.description: Defaults that apply to every contract.

baseline.description:
The baseline of known violations, which `zenith check` ignores so that
only new violations fail it.

cache.description:
The cache of what zenith found in each file on earlier runs, which
lets it skip reading and parsing the files that haven't changed since.

contracts.description:
The architecture contracts, keyed by id. Ids may contain ASCII
letters, digits, `-` and `_`, and are what `--contract`, the baseline
and `zenith-ignore` comments refer to.

title: zenith.toml
description:
The configuration of a zenith project. It lives at the project root, which
all of its paths are relative to.

include.description:
Globs of the files to scan. Defaults to every JavaScript and
TypeScript file, `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}`.

tsconfig.description:
Which `tsconfig.json` files to use: `"auto"` (the default) uses the
nearest one of each file, `"off"` uses none, and any other value is
the path of the one to use for every file.

conditions.description:
The condition names to match in `exports` maps, replacing the
defaults: `types`, `source`, `import`, `module`, `require`, `node`
and `default`. Conditions are matched in the order that each package
lists them.

main_fields.description:
The `package.json` fields that point at a package's entry point,
replacing the defaults: `module`, then `main`.

extensions.description:
The extensions to try, in order, when a specifier has none, replacing
the defaults: `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.d.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.js`, `.jsx`,
`.mjs`, `.cjs` and `.json`.

alias.description:
Bundler-only aliases: a specifier prefix, and the path that it maps
to.

ignore_unresolved.description:
Name patterns of specifiers that are expected not to resolve, so are
not reported as unresolved, e.g. `"/*"` for files served from a public
directory, or `"virtual:*"`.

include.description: Globs of the files to scan. Defaults to every Go file, `**/*.go`.

ignore_unresolved.description:
Name patterns of import paths that are expected not to resolve, so
are not reported as unresolved.

include.description:
Globs of the files to scan. Defaults to every Python file and stub,
`**/*.py` and `**/*.pyi`.

roots.description:
The directories that absolute imports start from, relative to the
project root, as on `sys.path`. Defaults to the `src` directory of each
package with a `pyproject.toml`, or the package's own directory when it
has none, and the project root.

ignore_unresolved.description:
Name patterns of module paths that are expected not to resolve, so
are not reported as unresolved.

include.description: Globs of the files to scan. Defaults to every Rust file, `**/*.rs`.

ignore_unresolved.description:
Name patterns of paths that are expected not to resolve, so are not
reported as unresolved, e.g. `"generated::*"` for a module that a
macro declares.

include.description:
Globs of the files to scan. Defaults to every Terraform, OpenTofu and
Terragrunt file: `**/*.tf`, `**/*.tofu` and `**/terragrunt.hcl`.

ignore_unresolved.description:
Name patterns of module sources and dependency paths that are expected
not to resolve, so are not reported as unresolved.

registries.description:
Name patterns of hosts that serve the public registry's modules, such
as a mirror, whose modules are named as the public registry's are,
besides the public registries themselves.

repository_hosts.description:
Name patterns of hosts of repositories that module sources may name
without a scheme, as they name GitHub's, such as a GitHub Enterprise
server, besides `github.com` and `bitbucket.org`.

bucket_hosts.description:
Name patterns of hosts of buckets that module sources may name without
a scheme, as they name S3's, besides `*.amazonaws.com` and
`www.googleapis.com`.

exclude.description:
Globs of files and directories to skip, on top of the default
excludes, such as `node_modules` and `.next`.

respect_gitignore.description:
Whether to skip the files that `.gitignore`, `.ignore` and the global
git excludes ignore.

FilesTable.description: Which files to scan for imports, whatever their language.

LanguagesTable.description: The languages to scan, each in a table of its own.

js.description: JavaScript and TypeScript: how their files are found and their imports resolved.

typescript.description: Another name for `js`. Giving both is an error.

go.description: Go: how its files are found and their imports resolved.

python.description: Python: how its files are found and the imports between its modules resolved.

rust.description: Rust: how its files are found and the imports between its crates and modules resolved.

terraform.description: Terraform, OpenTofu and Terragrunt: how their files are found and their module sources resolved.

exclude_kinds.description:
The import kinds that contracts ignore unless they set their own
`exclude_kinds`, e.g. `["type"]` to exempt type-only imports.

reexports.description:
How contracts see the imports of pass-through modules, the files that
only re-export other modules, unless they set their own `reexports`.

AnalysisTable.description: Defaults that apply to every contract.

oneOf.description:
A static value import or re-export: `import x from "s"`, `import "s"`,
`export * from "s"`.

A type-only import that is erased at runtime: `import type`, an
import whose specifiers are all `type`, or `typeof import("s")`.
A dynamic `import("s")` with a literal specifier.
A CommonJS `require("s")` or TypeScript `import x = require("s")`.

ImportKind.description:
How an import is made. Contracts can exclude imports of given kinds, e.g.
to exempt type-only imports.

oneOf.description:
An import of a pass-through module imports it, and so every module
it re-exports.

An import of names from a pass-through module imports the modules that
define them, as a bundler that leaves out unused modules loads them.

Reexports.description:
How a contract sees the imports of pass-through modules, the files that only
re-export other modules.

path.description: The path of the baseline file.

stale.description:
How to report baseline entries whose import no longer exists:
`"error"` fails the check, so that the baseline can only shrink, and
`"warn"` reports a warning.

oneOf.description: Stale entries fail the check, so the baseline can only shrink.
Stale entries are reported as warnings.

StaleLevel.description: How to report baseline entries whose import no longer exists.

enabled.description: Whether to use the cache. `--no-cache` turns it off for one run.

dir.description:
The directory to keep the cache in. Zenith creates it, with a
`.gitignore` that ignores everything in it.

CacheTable.description: The cache of what zenith found in each file on earlier runs.

from.description: The modules that must not import the `to` modules.

to.description:
The modules that must not be imported. External packages (`npm:`)
and builtins (`node:`, `bun:`) are allowed, with `js` enabled.

allow_indirect_imports.description:
If `true`, only direct imports count, rather than chains of
imports too.

boundaries.description:
Modules that chains of imports may start or end at, but not pass
through, e.g. `{ path = "web/**", directive = "use server" }`:
client code that imports a server function gets a reference to
it, not the code that it imports. Has no effect on direct imports,
so it can't be set with `allow_indirect_imports`.

name.description: The title shown in output. Defaults to the contract id.

severity.description:
`"warn"` reports the contract without failing the check when it
is broken, for gradual rollout.

exclude_kinds.description:
Import kinds to ignore, e.g. `["type"]` to exempt type-only
imports. Defaults to `[analysis] exclude_kinds`.

reexports.description:
How to see the imports of pass-through modules, the files that only
re-export other modules: `"opaque"`, an import of a pass-through module
imports every module it re-exports, or `"transparent"`, an
import of names from it imports the modules that define them.
Defaults to `[analysis] reexports`.

ignore_imports.description:
Imports to ignore, as `"<selector> -> <selector>"`: the direct
imports from the first selector's modules to the second's are
removed before checking.

unmatched_ignore_imports.description:
How to report an `ignore_imports` entry that matches no import:
`"error"` breaks the contract, `"warn"` reports a warning, and
`"none"` says nothing.

guidance.description: Text shown under the violations, e.g. how to fix them.

oneOf.description:
The `from` modules must not import the `to` modules, directly or
through other modules.

layers.description:
The layers, from highest to lowest. Higher layers may import lower
layers, never the reverse.

containers.description:
If set, the layers are paths relative to each container, and each
container is checked on its own.

exhaustive.description:
Whether every child of every container must be declared as a
layer. Requires `containers`.

exhaustive_ignores.description:
Children exempt from `exhaustive`: name patterns matched against
the base name with or without its JS/TS extension, so `index`
matches `index.ts`. The index files of the enabled languages, such
as Rust's `lib.rs`, `main.rs` and `mod.rs`, are always exempt.

skip.description: Modules whose children are not checked.

entrypoints.description:
Globs, relative to each module, of the files that code outside it
may import. They ignore JS/TS extensions, so `index` matches
`index.ts`, and match files only: `public/**` exposes a directory.

allowed_importers.description:

tests.

modules.description: The modules whose imports are counted, each on its own.

max_fan_in.description:
The most files outside each module that may import it. A file
counts once, however many of the module's files it imports.

max_fan_out.description:
The most files and packages of the project outside each module
that it may import. External packages and builtins don't count. A
file or package counts once, however many of the module's files
import it.

ContractTable.description: An architecture contract. Its `type` says what it checks.

SelectorValue.description:
A selector of modules: a path glob such as `web/src/domains/*`, a
workspace package (`pkg:@acme/*`), an external package (`npm:react`), a
builtin (`node:*` or `bun:*`), or a table that filters one. External
packages and builtins belong to the `js` language, which must be enabled.

path.description: The selector, in any of its string forms.

except.description: Selectors of modules to remove from each matched module.

directive.description:
Keep only the files that start with this directive, such as
`"use client"`, each as a module of its own.

oneOf.description: A broken contract fails the check.
A broken contract is reported without failing the check.

Severity.description: How severe a broken contract is.

oneOf.description: The contract is broken.
A warning is reported.
Nothing is reported.

AlertLevel.description: How to report an `ignore_imports` entry that matches no import.

LayerValue.description:
A layer of a `layers` contract: `"a"`, `"a | b"` for independent siblings
that may not import each other, `"a : b"` for siblings that may, and
`"(a)"` for a member that may be missing. Members are selectors.

layer.description: The layer, in its string form.

closed.description:
Whether the layer is closed: the layers above it may not import the
layers below it.
